In this work, we utilize the Gabor filter method to extract texture features in an orchard setting. Gabor filter/wavelet is widely used to extract texture features from the images for image retrieval and has been found to be very efficient ( Zhang et al., 2000 ). However, out of the many literature we reviewed ( Makem et al., 2020; Mede et al., 2018; Serrano et al., 2010; Shen and Bai, 2006; Zhang and Tan, 2002 ), none attempted to implement this method in an orchard environment, espe - cially for robot navigation. The closest work that adopted the Gabor filter in a semi-structured environment was by ( Alharbi et al., 2018 ) to develop a classifier for automatic counting of wheat spikes from wheat growth images. Gabor filters rely on the theory fronted by Campbell and Robson (1968) , which holds that the visual system decomposes the retinal image into several filtered images, each containing intensity variations over a narrow range of frequency (size) and orientation. In this work, a bank of 2D Gabor filters was explored. The 2D Gabor function comprises a si - nusoidal plane wave with frequency and orientation, which is modu - lated by a 2D Gaussian envelope. For an image frame H x , y having size x x y captured by the robot camera, the responsive impulse of a Gabor filter is computed using Eq (4) . H ’ x , y = exp { � 1 2 ( x 2 β 2 x + y 2 β 2 y ) } cos ( 2 π μ 0 x + ϕ ) (4) where μ 0 and ϕ represent the frequency and phase of the sinusoidal plane wave along the x-axis or 0 0 orientation, and β x and β y represent the space constants of the Gaussian envelope along the x- and y-axis, respectively. Depending on the image size, after the application of the Gabor filter, several features are produced that may cause too much load during analysis. 2.4.2.2. Principal Component analysis (PCA). For each pixel 34 features were extracted by Gabor filter. Hence, to minimize the computational demand during processing, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) tech - nique was employed. The central idea of PCA is to reduce the dimen - sionality of a data set having a large number of interrelated variables while retaining as much as possible of the variation present in the data set. PCA generates a new set of orthogonal features known as principal components by transforming several interrelated variables ( Jolliffe and Cadima, 2016 ) hence eliminating redundancies. chunks.text: for autonomous navigation was explored by Ali et al. (2008) . Additionally, Radcliffe et al. (2018) developed a machine vision navigation system for a small-unmanned ground vehicle in an orchard using the sky and the canopy as the primary focus for navigation path generation. This technique avoided the effect of weeds (color) during segmentation. Ponnambalam et al. (2020) studied an adaptive multi- ROI method aimed at fitting trajectories within drivable regions in Strawberry Fields. An open-loop field test approach with a real agri - cultural robot demonstrated favorable comparability of their approach to other traditional path generation approaches. Under vision based navigation systems, camera-based systems are the most cost effective technique in comparison to other techniques like LIDER and Radar based systems. ( Islam et al., 2018 ). Developing a real-time fully functional navigation system for autonomous guidance is quite a grueling task due to the dynamic nature of agricultural fields for instance, non-uniform terrain, weeds condi - tions, changing weather conditions, varied illumination among others ( Hague et al., 2000; Shalal et al., 2013 ). In vision-based navigation systems, these factors make it very cumbersome to segment the scene, which is the first and critical step in path generation( Chen et al., 2020 ). Moreover, in several related studies the developed algorithms first extracted the tree rows ( He et al., 2010 ) before extracting the guidance path. In contrast, the proposed algorithm in our work only uses the bi - nary image and extracts the navigation path hence reducing the computation load on the system. Motivated by these factors, this study is aimed at developing a novel machine vision system for autonomous inter-row navigation for agricultural robot based on medial axis detec - tion. We deviate from the conventional RGB segmentation and employ Gabor filter banks alongside principal component analysis techniques. The main objective of the current study is to generate an accurate navigation path for an autonomous robot in a dynamic orchard setting. Specific objectives include; a) to develop effective, robust, and accurate path segmentation based on Gabor filter, b) To extract the region of interest (ROI) from the segmented path and c) To extract the medial axis for robot navigation. This paper is organized as follows: Section 2 details the materials and methods employed to achieve the research objective. In Section 3, experimental results and discussion on the proposed technique are presented. Finally, in Section 4, the conclusion and future work is provided. 2. Material and methods 2.1. Vehicle platform This work employed the use of a tracked orchard robot designed and Fig. 1. Tracked orchard robot platform (a) front view (b) side view. S. Opiyo et al. Computers and Electronics in Agriculture 185 (2021) 106153 3 developed at the college of engineering of Nanjing Agricultural Uni - versity, Jiangsu Province, Nanjing China. The platform consists of tracks and uses skid steering technique. Two driving motors (AC Servo Motor 60ST-M01930, 380 V) were separately attached to drive the left and the right tracks via servo drive (ASDD-30A) from Taizhou Yifeng Electronics co. LTD. The dimensions of the platform are; 2.60 m long 1.25 m wide and 1.20 m height. To enable smooth operation in an orchard bearing in mind the rugged terrain, the platform is raised 0.40 m above the ground. The weight of the robot, 700 kg, is well spread over the entire platform, and the wide base ensures stability of the vehicle platform. Fig. 1 shows the vehicle platform used in this work. The central onboard processor is an industrial computer with an Intel Core i5, 2.4 GHz CPU with 8 GB DDR3 RAM.
